title: Queueing in continuous integration
summary: CI workflow runs as customers of a queueing system: when they arrive, how long they stay, how many are in the system, and the conservation law that ties the three.

concepts.label: Workflow run
concepts.description: One execution of a GitHub Actions workflow, triggered by a push, pull request or schedule.

facts.text: GitHub lists a repository's runs at /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs, filterable by created date.

children.label: Workflow
children.description: The workflow definition a run belongs to (Linux tests, Wheel builder, …).

children.label: Job
children.description: A unit of a run that takes one runner; a run has several.

concepts.label: Queueing system
concepts.description: Items arriving, waiting, being served and leaving.

children.label: Time in system
children.description: W, from start to last update, minutes.

children.label: Number in system
children.description: L(t), runs in flight at each minute, and its time average.

children.label: Little's law
children.description: L = λW for any stable system over a long window.

children.label: Runner capacity
children.description: How many jobs can run at once; queue time grows sharply as utilisation nears it.

children.label: Queue time
children.description: Time a job waits for a runner (jobs API).
